text:
alex: Heads-up — after kernel v3.7.1 rolled to canary we observed a ~12% p95 latency regression for Llama-2-13B on 2048 context. Throughput steady but tail is worse. posting quick numbers and profiling callouts.

alex: baseline (kernel v3.6.4, kvcache-enabled): p50=85ms p95=310ms throughput=180 tokens/s (batch=4, ctx=2048)
alex: new (kernel v3.7.1, same config): p50=88ms p95=348ms throughput=176 tokens/s

alex: flamegraphs point at attention kernel switching path — more time in kernel-dispatch and memcpy for heads>64 models.

jing: thanks, pinged infra. do we have per-kernel selection logs? can we repro with perf-bot sweep? :mag:

perf-bot: Scheduled micro-sweep: llm=llama-2-13b, ctx=2048, batches=[1,2,4,8], runs=10 per config. Will attach traces. ETA ~10m.

maria: curious if RoPE scaling codepath changed default scaling factor in 3.7.1 — that can increase KV cache footprint, causing extra memcpy. iirc we saw similar behavior when head_dim changed -> more fragmentation.

alex: confirmed: RoPE scaling unchanged, but kernel selector now prefers fused-attn-v2 for certain seq_len/batch combos which added an intermediate staging buffer. that buffer shows up in heap and increases memcopies for heads=96 and kv_dim=128.

sam: quick notes from sweep (raw):
```
# summary (median over runs)
batch=1: p95=420ms
batch=2: p95=360ms
batch=4: p95=348ms
batch=8: p95=410ms
```
sam: pattern: sweet spot at batch=4 for throughput/latency tradeoff on 13B with 2k ctx. larger batches degrade tail because fused kernel fallback triggers.

jing: actionables I see: 1) tighten kernel selector rule so fused-attn-v2 only chosen when seq_len<1024 or heads<=32; 2) add post-selection check for extra staging buffer size and prefer fallback if staging > 1MB for low-latency tier.

maria: model-specific recommendations we should document in console:
- Llama-2-13B: prefer kernel=auto but override to "fused-attn-v1" for ctx>=1536 and heads>=64; max_batch=4 for latency-sensitive routes.
- Mistral-7B / Mixtral: safe to use fused-attn-v2, but cap batch at 8 and enable aggressive KV cache reuse (prefix caching) to reduce repeated memcpy.
- Qwen-family: use explicit rope_scale=1.0 (no auto-scaling) on long ctx to avoid extra kv reshaping; if using rope-scaling, run a memory-prefetch option.

alex: adding a small config snippet for runtime flags to test: 
```
runtime.configs.add({
  "model":"llama-2-13b",
  "kernel_selector":"prefer:fused-attn-v1",
  "max_batch":4,
  "kv_cache":true,
  "kv_prefetch":true
})
```

sam: repro checklist for eng-runtime:
- run perf-bot sweep with kernel v3.6.4 and v3.7.1 (done)
- capture per-kernel memcopy counts and staging buffer sizes (perf-bot attached traces)
- test with heads/kv_dim permutations: heads=[32,64,96], kv_dim=[64,128,256]

perf-bot: uploaded traces: link=https://perf.s3/redwood/1750456789/traces.tar.gz (contains flamegraphs + kernel selection logs)

maria: quick observation from traces: for heads=96, kv_dim=128 the staging buffer average=1.6MB on v3.7.1 vs 320KB on v3.6.4 — that explains extra memcpy time.

jing: tentative hotfix: revert the path that enabled extra staging for fused-attn-v2 and add a heuristic: if (staging_size > 1MB && latency_slo=="p95<350ms") choose fallback-kernel. i'll draft PR.

alex: sounds good. also we should add two console knobs: (A) per-model kernel override (B) kernel-staging threshold in bytes with default 1MB. ops can tune per-customer.

maria: long-term: consider kernel memory layout optimizer that reuses the pre-allocated KV scratch to avoid per-request alloc/free — that would help Qwen and Llama with large heads. filing RFC.

alex: final note for docs: add a short section "Model tuning cheat sheet" with recommended batch limits, kernel hints, and rope scaling notes. i'll draft a PR and link to perf traces.

jing: assigned to me for kernel-selector PR, assigning to maria for docs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
